assertions.text: Every @TableTest function is declared inside a type (a struct, class, enum or an extension of one), not at file scope.
Test function body contains no if, guard or switch statement and no ternary
No @TableTest function body defaults a value with ??, or calls .map, .flatMap or .compactMap on one of its parameters.
assertions.evidence: 1 @TableTest function(s); no ?? and no .map on a parameter

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Text?')

LoanReminder.text(for:) calls a function or a computed property of the app that decides the reminder, and a @TableTest calls that function with rows on both sides of the 3-day, the due-date and the 30-day line (4 and 3, 0 and -1, -29 and -30). FAILS when the decision stays inside text(for:), and when the new function is a copy that text(for:) does not call.

No cell of a @TableTest table is longer than 100 characters. The table holds the decision as data, and a reader reviews the wording. FAILS on a single long cell, since one long cell makes the whole table wide.

Outside the @TableTest tables, the tests hold at most one string literal longer than 100 characters. A person reads the wording, so a copy of a constant sentence only checks that the two copies agree. One sentence can be the wiring check. FAILS on a test for each sentence.
assertions.evidence: 1 string literal(s) over 100 characters outside the tables (at most 1)

assertions.text: No init(from:) is written into the app code under Sources/.
swift build --build-tests succeeds against the package scaffolding
The tests pass when run against LoanReminder
The eval's own tests pass against the changed app code: text(for:) gives the same text as before on both sides of each line, also for a reserved item.
